sources.name: Zimbabwe Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education Chemistry Syllabus, Forms 5–6 (2024–2030)
sources.note: A web transcription of a document bearing the Ministry's name, not an officially authenticated source. Topic-level mappings are editorial, not official objective codes.

objectives.title: Mole & stoichiometry
objectives.competency: Translate between mass, amount and particle ratios.

objectives.title: Limiting reagents
objectives.competency: Determine a limiting reagent from stoichiometric amounts.

objectives.title: Atomic structure
objectives.competency: Interpret electron configurations and periodic trends.

objectives.title: Bonding & shapes

objectives.title: Energetics

objectives.title: Electrochemistry

objectives.title: Equilibrium constants
objectives.competency: Construct and calculate equilibrium constants.

objectives.title: Equilibrium position
objectives.competency: Distinguish kinetics from equilibrium shifts.

objectives.title: Acids & bases
objectives.competency: Calculate the pH of dilute strong acids.

objectives.title: Reaction kinetics
objectives.competency: Determine orders from initial rate experiments.

objectives.title: Period 3 trends
objectives.competency: Explain atomic size and ionisation trends.

objectives.title: Group II
objectives.competency: Identify solubility trends in Group II compounds.

objectives.title: Group IV
objectives.competency: Explain bonding and structure of Group IV oxides.

objectives.title: Halogens
objectives.competency: Predict halogen displacement reactions.

objectives.title: Industrial nitrogen

objectives.title: Alkene chemistry

objectives.title: Halogenoalkanes
objectives.competency: Identify nucleophilic substitution and reagents.

objectives.title: Alcohol oxidation

objectives.title: Carbonyl tests

objectives.title: Acyl derivatives
objectives.competency: Predict products of acyl chloride reactions.

objectives.title: Polymerisation

objectives.title: Transition-metal complexes
objectives.competency: Relate ligands and d orbitals to complex colour.

objectives.title: Chromatography
objectives.competency: Interpret chromatography and retention factors.

objectives.title: Environmental chemistry

objectives.title: Nanochemistry

objectives.title: Titration data
objectives.competency: Identify concordant titres and calculate their mean.

objectives.title: Qualitative analysis
objectives.competency: Infer ions and gases from characteristic tests.

objectives.title: Experimental planning
objectives.competency: Identify variables and design valid tests.

questions.stem: A sample contains 0.25 mol of Na₂CO₃. What amount of sodium ions does it contain?
questions.explanation: Each formula unit contains two Na⁺ ions, so 0.25 × 2 = 0.50 mol of Na⁺.

questions.stem: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. A mixture contains 0.20 mol Mg and 0.30 mol HCl. What is the maximum amount of MgCl₂ formed?
questions.explanation: HCl is limiting: 0.30 mol HCl makes 0.30/2 = 0.15 mol MgCl₂.

questions.stem: What is the ground-state electron configuration of a chlorine atom (atomic number 17)?
questions.explanation: A neutral chlorine atom has 17 electrons: 2 + 2 + 6 + 2 + 5 = 17.

questions.stem: What are the shape and approximate bond angle in NH₃?
questions.explanation: Three bonding pairs and one lone pair around nitrogen give a trigonal pyramidal molecular shape.

questions.stem: Using ΔH°c(CH₄) = −890, ΔH°c(C) = −394 and ΔH°c(H₂) = −286 kJ mol⁻¹, calculate ΔH°f(CH₄) in kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation: C(s) + 2H₂(g) → CH₄(g). By Hess’s law: −394 + 2(−286) − (−890) = −76 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V. What is E°cell for the Zn/Cu galvanic cell?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode = +0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V.

questions.stem: For N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), [NO₂] = 0.20 mol dm⁻³ and [N₂O₄] = 0.10 mol dm⁻³ at equilibrium. Calculate numerical Kc.
questions.explanation: Kc = [NO₂]²/[N₂O₄] = (0.20)²/0.10 = 0.40 mol dm⁻³.

questions.stem: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH < 0. What happens to the equilibrium constant Kc if temperature increases?

choices.text: It stays the same but rate increases.

questions.explanation: Heating favours the endothermic reverse reaction, so Kc decreases for the exothermic forward reaction.

questions.stem: What is the pH of 0.010 mol dm⁻³ HCl at 25 °C, treating it as fully dissociated?
questions.explanation: pH = −log₁₀[H⁺] = −log₁₀(0.010) = 2.

questions.stem: In a rate experiment, doubling [A] while holding other concentrations constant causes the initial rate to quadruple. What is the order with respect to A?
questions.explanation: The rate rises by a factor of four on doubling [A]: 4 = 2ⁿ, hence n = 2.

questions.stem: Which best explains the general decrease in atomic radius from Na to Cl across Period 3?

choices.text: Increasing nuclear charge with broadly similar shielding
The atoms lose all valence electrons

questions.explanation: Across the period, proton number rises but valence electrons enter the same shell, increasing attraction.

questions.stem: Which Group II sulphate is least soluble in water?
questions.explanation: Sulphate solubility generally decreases down Group II.

questions.stem: Why does SiO₂ have a much higher melting point than CO₂?

choices.text: SiO₂ has a giant covalent network; CO₂ consists of simple molecules
SiO₂ has only weak van der Waals forces
CO₂ is ionic and SiO₂ is metallic

questions.explanation: Melting SiO₂ requires breaking many strong covalent bonds; melting CO₂ overcomes intermolecular forces.

questions.stem: What happens when chlorine water is added to aqueous potassium bromide?

choices.text: Bromine forms by oxidation of Br⁻

questions.explanation: Cl₂ + 2Br⁻ → 2Cl⁻ + Br₂. Chlorine oxidises bromide ions.

questions.stem: In the Haber process, what does an iron catalyst change?

choices.text: The forward and reverse reaction rates

questions.explanation: A catalyst accelerates both directions and shortens the time to equilibrium; it does not shift the equilibrium.

questions.stem: Which reaction causes bromine water to lose its orange colour when mixed with ethene?
questions.explanation: Br₂ adds across the carbon-carbon double bond to form 1,2-dibromoethane.

questions.stem: What is the main organic product when bromoethane is heated with aqueous NaOH?
questions.explanation: OH⁻ substitutes for Br in CH₃CH₂Br to give CH₃CH₂OH.

questions.stem: What product results from oxidising propan-2-ol using acidified potassium dichromate(VI)?
questions.explanation: Secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones; propan-2-ol gives propanone.

questions.stem: Which observation supports the presence of an aldehyde rather than a ketone when using Tollens’ reagent?
questions.explanation: Aldehydes reduce ammoniacal silver(I) in Tollens’ reagent to Ag(s).

questions.stem: Ethanoyl chloride reacts with ethanol. What organic product forms?
questions.explanation: Acyl chloride + alcohol → ester + HCl. Here CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ forms.

questions.stem: Which statement describes condensation polymerisation?

choices.text: Every monomer must have a C=C bond
Polymer forms with elimination of a small molecule in typical condensation reactions
The reaction makes no covalent bonds

questions.explanation: Condensation polymerisation typically creates links such as ester or amide bonds with elimination of a small molecule.

questions.stem: Many transition-metal complexes are coloured primarily because visible light can promote:

choices.text: Transitions between split d-orbital energy levels

questions.explanation: Ligands split d-orbital energies. Absorbed light can promote electronic transitions between these levels, when allowed.

questions.stem: A spot travels 4.8 cm and the solvent front travels 8.0 cm. Calculate Rf for the spot.
questions.explanation: Rf = distance travelled by spot / distance travelled by solvent front = 4.8/8.0 = 0.60.

questions.stem: Which solid is commonly used as a source of calcium compounds for flue-gas desulphurisation?
questions.explanation: Limestone (CaCO₃) or its derived lime can react with acidic SO₂ in desulphurisation.

questions.stem: Why can a catalyst made of nanoparticles be effective even when its total mass is low?

choices.text: Their high surface-area-to-volume ratio exposes many active sites
They cannot participate in chemical reactions

questions.explanation: A large fraction of atoms are at exposed surfaces, potentially increasing accessible catalytic sites.

questions.stem: Concordant titres are 24.80 cm³ and 24.85 cm³; a third titre is 25.40 cm³. Calculate the mean of concordant titres to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: (24.80 + 24.85)/2 = 24.825 cm³, reported to 2 d.p. as 24.83 cm³ (ordinary half-up rounding).

questions.stem: A solid effervesces with dilute acid. The gas turns limewater milky. Which anion is indicated?
questions.explanation: Carbonate + acid releases CO₂, which forms CaCO₃ precipitate in limewater.

questions.stem: To determine how temperature affects reaction rate, which variable should normally be kept constant?
questions.explanation: Keep conditions other than temperature, including concentrations, constant to isolate the temperature effect.

questions.stem: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) is exothermic. Explain why raising temperature decreases the equilibrium yield of NH₃. [3 marks]

rubric.text: Identify the forward formation of NH₃ as exothermic.
State that a temperature increase favours the endothermic reverse reaction.
Conclude that the equilibrium shifts towards reactants, decreasing NH₃ yield.

questions.explanation: Heat favours the endothermic reverse reaction, so at the new equilibrium less ammonia is present. Faster rates do not by themselves explain the shift.

questions.stem: A catalyst increases the rate of a reversible reaction. Explain the effect on activation energy and equilibrium position. [3 marks]

rubric.text: Catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway.
The alternative pathway has a lower activation energy.
The equilibrium position and Kc are unchanged (both directions speed up).

questions.explanation: Catalysts lower the activation barrier for both directions but do not change thermodynamic equilibrium.

questions.stem: Explain why the first ionisation energy of aluminium is lower than that of magnesium, even though aluminium has more protons. [3 marks]

rubric.text: Mg outer electron is in a 3s orbital while Al first removed electron is in 3p.
The 3p electron is higher in energy (and/or better shielded) than the 3s electron.
Consequently the Al 3p electron is easier to remove despite greater nuclear charge.

questions.explanation: The electron lost from Al is in 3p rather than Mg 3s, producing the well-known Period 3 exception.

questions.stem: Explain why aqueous NaOH reacting with bromoethane gives a different principal product from hot ethanolic NaOH. [3 marks]

rubric.text: Aqueous OH⁻ promotes nucleophilic substitution.
The aqueous reaction forms ethanol.
Hot ethanolic base promotes elimination of HBr, forming ethene.

questions.explanation: The solvent and conditions influence the competition between substitution and elimination.

questions.stem: Describe one industrial chemical method for removing SO₂ from flue gases, including a reagent, chemistry and environmental benefit. [3 marks]

rubric.text: Identify an appropriate calcium-based sorbent such as limestone/lime.
Explain conversion of SO₂ to calcium sulphite and/or sulphate (oxidation can occur).
State that this reduces release of SO₂ and therefore acid-rain-forming pollution.

questions.explanation: Wet limestone scrubbing captures SO₂ as calcium-containing products, reducing atmospheric release.

questions.stem: A learner wishes to investigate how concentration changes the rate of reaction between calcium carbonate and hydrochloric acid. State four design features supporting a valid comparison. [4 marks]

rubric.text: Change the concentration of HCl as the independent variable.
Keep the mass and surface area/particle size of calcium carbonate constant.
Keep other conditions such as temperature and total reaction volume constant.
Measure rate comparably, e.g. CO₂ volume against time using suitable apparatus.

questions.explanation: Control variables while systematically varying acid concentration and measuring gas production versus time.

questions.stem: Explain how to confirm that a gas produced by adding dilute acid to a carbonate is CO₂. [3 marks]

rubric.text: Add dilute acid to the suspected carbonate to produce the gas.
Bubble the gas through clear limewater.
Limewater turns milky as a precipitate of calcium carbonate forms.

questions.explanation: CO₂ forms CaCO₃(s) in limewater, giving milky cloudiness.

questions.stem: How many moles of CO₂ are produced by complete combustion of 0.75 mol of propane (C₃H₈)? Enter the numerical value.
questions.explanation: C₃H₈ + 5O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O; n(CO₂) = 3 × 0.75 = 2.25 mol.

questions.stem: Calculate the pH of 0.0010 mol dm⁻³ HNO₃ at 25 °C (complete dissociation).
questions.explanation: For complete dissociation, [H⁺] = 10⁻³ mol dm⁻³ and pH = −log₁₀(10⁻³) = 3.

questions.stem: For an exothermic gas equilibrium producing fewer moles of gas, which combination generally favours product yield?
questions.explanation: Lower temperature favours the exothermic forward process; higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules.

questions.stem: Under reflux with excess acidified dichromate(VI), what is the main oxidation product of propan-1-ol?
questions.explanation: A primary alcohol is oxidised through the aldehyde to a carboxylic acid under strong reflux conditions.

questions.stem: Explain why many transition-metal aqua complexes absorb visible light and appear coloured. [3 marks]

rubric.text: Surrounding ligands split the metal ion d-orbitals into different energy levels.
Light of suitable energy is absorbed to promote d-electron transitions.
The observed colour results from wavelengths not absorbed (transmitted/reflected).

questions.explanation: Ligand-field splitting allows visible-range absorption in suitable complexes. This is a model and not universal for all complexes.

questions.stem: A 25.0 cm³ sample of HCl is neutralised by 20.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH. Calculate the HCl concentration in mol dm⁻³.
Which pair can produce a polyester by condensation polymerisation?

choices.text: A diol and a dicarboxylic acid

questions.explanation: A diol and a dicarboxylic acid can form repeating ester linkages with water eliminated.

questions.stem: For 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), which expression is Kc?
questions.explanation: Each exponent is the corresponding coefficient in the balanced chemical equation.

questions.stem: State Hess’s law and give two conditions or principles that explain why it is valid. [3 marks]

rubric.text: State that total enthalpy change is independent of the reaction path for the same initial and final states.
Mention enthalpy is a state function.
Mention energy conservation or the importance of comparing the same overall initial and final conditions.

questions.explanation: The enthalpy change depends only on the initial and final states; this follows from state-function behaviour and conservation of energy.
